editorial:
Imagine moving into a cheap, run-down apartment with your young daughter, hoping for a fresh start, only to find out the place is falling apart. You start noticing weird leaks in the ceiling and hearing strange noises that just won't stop. The vibe is super creepy and damp, making you feel like something is watching you from the shadows. You follow the main character, Dahlia, as she tries to protect her kid while figuring out why this building feels so wrong. It is not about jump scares, but more about that slow feeling of dread that makes you want to keep the lights on.

The acting is great and really makes you care about the bond between the mother and daughter. While the story moves a bit slowly at times, the mystery keeps you guessing until the end. If you like ghost stories that feel more like a sad mystery than a slasher flick, you will love this. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the gritty details of the apartment. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move for a rainy night.
endingExplained: You find out the ghost is a little girl who was left behind and died in the building. She is looking for her mother and tries to take Dahlia's daughter to replace her own. In the end, Dahlia realizes the only way to save her child is to give herself up. She hugs her daughter one last time and lets the ghost take her instead, sacrificing her own life to keep her daughter safe.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves ghost stories with a sad twist.
